scenes.visual: Big navy hook text pops word by word; Norb peeks curious from below.
scenes.cardText: Why does one bad comment ruin your day?
scenes.voiceover: Why does one bad comment ruin your whole day?

scenes.visual: A balance beam: one big coral BAD block on the left tips the beam down, outweighing five small teal good blocks on the right.
scenes.voiceover: Your brain doesn't treat bad and good equally. One bad thing outweighs several good things, every time.

scenes.visual: Two bars under BRAIN WEIGHT: a very tall coral '1 BAD' bar towers over a short teal '5 GOOD' bar.
scenes.voiceover: A single criticism can undo five compliments. Your brain is wired to make threats stick harder than wins.

scenes.visual: A small teal dot breathes at center while slow mustard rings expand outward and a circular timer fills — savoring a good moment.
scenes.voiceover: Good things slide off. So force a pause — thirty seconds to sit with something good makes the brain hold on.

scenes.visual: THE SCIENCE card; below it the balance beam tips toward the single heavy coral block — bad weighed deeper than good.
scenes.cardText: Negativity bias: bad events are processed more deeply than equally strong good ones.
scenes.voiceover: Negativity bias: research shows bad events trigger stronger neural responses than equally intense good ones — built-in threat detection from our past.

scenes.visual: TRY THIS card; below it the savor animation plays — teal dot breathing as mustard rings expand. Norb celebrates.
scenes.cardText:
When something good happens, pause.
30 seconds — really feel it.
scenes.voiceover: When something good happens today, pause for thirty seconds and actually feel it. That's your antidote.
